_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for DA's built-in Translate app config on aemgdc/aemdev.
*** THIS FILE IS ANNOTATED SOURCE, NOT THE PAYLOAD. ***
`npm run tx:config` MUST strip every `_comment` (top level and per sheet) and every
`_why` (per row) before POSTing. Two different reasons, both non-obvious:
- A DA sheet document may carry ONLY `:`-prefixed top-level keys or
{total,limit,offset,data} sheet objects. `_comment` is neither, so the write is
refused by the content bus — and it is refused at PREVIEW, not at
admin.da.live, so DA is left holding a file every reader 404s.
- `_why` inside a data row becomes a real sheet COLUMN. It would show up in the
sheet UI and be handed to the connector as data.
The annotations live here because a rule table nobody can read is a rule table
nobody maintains — the reasoning is worth more in git than the payload is.
Pushed to DA at /aemgdc/aemdev/.da/translate.json by `npm run tx:config -- --apply`.
DA resolves this path first, then /aemgdc/.da/translate.json, then the bundled
Google-connector default. Schema verified against adobe/da-nx at
nx/blocks/loc/connectors/google/translate.json, parsed by nx/blocks/loc/dnt/dnt.js
(parseConfig) — the public docs cover only the four `*.conflict.behavior` keys and
describe none of the other four sheets.
`custom-doc-rules.rule` is a near-English query parsed by nx/blocks/loc/dnt/
parseQuery.js. Grammar: directives `translate` | `dnt`; targets `row` / `col` /
`cell` with 1-BASED indices (ranges `1-4`, negatives count from the end, `*` = all);
operators `is`, `not-is`, `startswith`, `contains`, `has-element` and their `not-`
forms; `if` / `unless` introduce a condition. Column numbers refer to the AUTHORED
table, so they change if a block's authoring shape changes — that is the one way
these rules rot silently, because an out-of-range column is a no-op, not an error.
Default is TRANSLATE. A block absent from custom-doc-rules has all its prose sent.
So the rules below are the exceptions, and the bias is deliberate: forgetting to
list a prose block costs a little money, while forgetting to DNT a path or an
identifier silently corrupts a page in ten locales.

data.description: Pulling source content into the send-for-translation folder. `merge` so a hand-edit made in staging is not silently discarded by a re-sync.
Content returning FROM translation wins. This is machine translation into a tree nobody hand-edits before QA, so `merge` would only create phantom conflicts.

Rolling out to the locale. `merge` because by this point a native reviewer may have corrected the locale document, and a re-rollout must not throw that away — the review verdict in the tracker would then be attached to text that no longer exists.
Copying source into a region without translating.
Machine translation. Every locale is `Machine Translation` in the languages sheet below; the human pass is the tracker's native-review stage, not the connector's.

_comment: `code` is what the connector is told; `location` is the URL prefix. For the two
Chinese entries they differ in CASE ONLY (zh-CN vs /zh-cn) and that near-miss is
exactly the kind that fails silently — the connector accepts an unknown code and
hands back the source text untranslated. scripts/tracker/locales.js holds both
spellings per locale (`serviceCode` vs `code`) so one place knows the difference.
`en` is `Skip`, not `Translate`: it is the source.

data.rule: translate col 2 if col 1 is "title" or "description" or "displaydescription" or "og:title"
data._why: Only the prose metadata. Everything else in this block is machine-read: template, status, category, tags, robots, speakers, event-date, location, recap-video, author, image, publication-date. Translating `status` from `upcoming` to `bevorstehend` breaks the lifecycle model AND the query index in one step.
Pure layout directives — grid, columns, gap, spacing, background, color scheme. No prose at all.
A headless config block; blocks/header/header.js reads its key/value rows and removes it. Nothing here is ever displayed.

THE most important rule here. A translated identifier, flag, or shell command is not a lower-quality translation, it is a defect that produces broken instructions — and technical-articles is the group where this block appears most. The label row goes untranslated with it, which is the right trade for never corrupting the body.
The cell holds a document path. scripts/scripts.js auto-blocks any href containing /fragments/, so a translated path resolves to nothing and the fragment silently vanishes from the page.
Authored as | event label | title | youtube url |. Column 3 is the video URL. The label and the talk title do translate.

data.rule: dnt col 2 if col 1 is "index" or "limit" or "category" or "tag" or "template" or "path" or "status" or "card-1-url" or "card-2-url" or "card-3-url" or "card-4-url"
data._why: These blocks mix authored prose (badge, title, dek, cta) with query configuration. The config values are index paths, tag ids, template names and numbers — a translated `aemdev:category/meetup` matches nothing and the feed renders empty, which reads as a content problem rather than a translation one.

card-N-date is a rendered date string the feed prints verbatim; the locale tree wants a localized date, but a machine-translated one is unparseable rather than localized. Left in English until a real date-formatting pass exists.
Column 1 of the first row is the headshot image. Names and LinkedIn URLs are handled by dnt-content-rules and dnt-sheet-rules respectively.
Scheduled-content control rows — dates and paths driving when content appears.

Stated explicitly rather than left to the default, because `table`'s first authored row is consumed as a BLOCK NAME (see blocks/table/table.js) and it would be easy to add a `dnt row 1` rule here by analogy with other blocks. Don't: row 1 is a real header row by the time DA sees it.

data.block: carousel, advanced-tabs, columns, card, mtb-card, callout, pullquote, hero, home-hero, blog-post-hero, figure, step, ticker, update, qa
data._why: Prose blocks, listed explicitly so a reader of this sheet can see they were considered rather than forgotten. Same as the default.
Search scaffolding: labels translate, the paths and index references in them must not.

data.block: tracker-summary, translation-matrix, group-progress, work-queue, escalation-list, status-primer
data._why: The tracker's own boards. They live under /tracker/, which is never sent for translation at all — this rule is a second line of defence in case a /tracker/ path is ever added to a project by hand.

_comment: Literal strings wrapped in translate="no" wherever they appear in body text.
Two categories, both deliberate. PRODUCT AND EVENT NAMES are proper nouns whose
translation is a defect the judge is configured to fail — `Edge Delivery Services`
rendered as `Servicios de entrega perimetral` is wrong in every locale, and it is
the single most common machine-translation failure on a technical site.
PERSON NAMES are here because the meetups and bios groups make speaker names
load-bearing content, and a transliterated name into a CJK locale is both wrong
and hard to spot in review. This list must grow as bios are authored — the bios
roster sheet (/bios.json, column `Name`) is the source, and keeping the two in
step is a real maintenance cost. The alternative, translating names, is worse.
Note the matcher is a substring XPath contains(), so a short string here has wide
reach: do not add a common word.
Applied to sheet cells. Absolute URLs, site-root-relative paths, taxonomy tag ids
(`aemdev:topic/edge-delivery`), and the hash authoring language this site uses
(`#_blank`, `#_dnt`, `#_self` — see scripts/utils/link-target.js). Every one is an
identifier that must survive byte-identical.

data.dnt-columns: page-path, locale, locale-path, sent-at, previewed, online, translation-status, review-status, review-updated, subgroup, template, en-status, content-escalation

_comment: Row 1 covers the bios roster (/bios.json) — its structural columns. `Name` is NOT
listed here because it is covered by dnt-content-rules instead, which also catches
the name where it appears in body prose; a column rule would only catch the cell.
Row 2: the redirects sheet is entirely paths.
Row 3: every column of the tracker's own group sheets, as defence in depth. Those
sheets live under /tracker/ and are never in a translation project, but a status
value silently translated from `en-published` to `en-veröffentlicht` would not
fail loudly — it would classify as `unknown en-status` and quietly stop counting.
